examples: At nine tomorrow I will be driving to work. — I'll be driving to work.
She will not be working on Sunday. — She won't be working on Sunday.
— Will you be using the car tonight? — Yes, I will.

items.case: an action that will be in progress at a stated future time
examples: This time tomorrow we'll be flying over the Alps.
At eight o'clock tonight she'll be watching the match.

items.case: an action that will definitely happen as part of a routine or arrangement (instead of the Present Continuous)
examples: I'll be seeing Anna at the office tomorrow, so I can pass on your message.
We'll be meeting the team on Friday as usual.
items.hint: It is already planned, so the meeting is certain.

items.case: asking politely about someone's plans, to see if they can do something for us or so that we can offer help
examples: — Will you be passing the post office? — Yes. Why? — Could you post this letter for me?
Will you be using the printer this afternoon? I need it for an hour.
items.hint: We want to know whether our wishes fit in with their plans.
